interface.signature: def stringConversion(X: str, Y: str) -> int

preconditions.description: Both X and Y must be strings.
The lengths of X and Y are between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 1 if can_convert(X, Y) else return_value == 0
postconditions.description: Returns 1 if X can be converted to Y using the allowed operations, otherwise 0.

postconditions.expression: can_convert(X, Y) == (len(Y) > 0 and all(any((X[i].lower() == Y[j].lower() and (X[i].isupper() or Y[j].isupper())) or (X[i].isupper() and X[i] == Y[j])) for i in range(len(X))) for j in range(len(Y)))
postconditions.description: Conversion is possible if Y is non-empty and every character in Y can be matched to a character in X such that: (1) the characters match case-insensitively, and if the X character is lowercase, the Y character must be uppercase (implying the lowercase was converted), OR (2) the X character is already uppercase and matches Y exactly. Additionally, the matching must respect the relative order of characters in X and Y (subsequence property).
